consistency_issues.en: The Teshial are 'typical' in appearance for elves, but they could create the illusion of almost any appearance if they so choose. Some people even say that due to their enormous control of dreams they could shape their children as they wish, giving them human or even orcish appearance. On the other hand, even people who come up with such theories go silent when asked why an elf should choose to have a child that looks that way.
variants: Тешиалы выглядят как 'typical' для эльфов, но они могут создать иллюзию практически любого внешнего вида, если захотят. Некоторые люди даже говорят, что благодаря своему огромному контролю над снами они могли формировать своих детей по своему желанию, придавая им человеческий или даже орочий облик. С другой стороны, даже люди, выдвигающие подобные теории, молчат, когда их спрашивают, почему эльф должен иметь такого ребенка.

Тешиалы выглядят как 'typical' для эльфов, но они могут создать иллюзию практически любого внешнего вида, если захотят. С другой стороны, даже люди, выдвигающие подобные теории, молчат, когда их спрашивают, почему эльф должен иметь такого ребенка.

pl_reference_issues.en: The Howling Grotto of Nargor used to be a hideout for criminals in the early days when colonisation just started on the isles. Those criminals were probably the first pirates although is unlikely that they had more than a few fishing boats at their disposal. They built some rooms in the caverns but supposedly they found evidence of prior attempts to use the grotto in some way and some of the caverns seemed to be not natural. For some reasons they were attracted to the lower caves where the howling of the wind was that fierce that people said it could drive a man crazy. Be that as it may, those first pirates were known for their bloodthirst, their frequent infightings and for torturing their prisoners. It is assumed that they all killed themselves in their madness. The grotto is rumoured to be haunted by the ghosts of these pirates and those of their victims - but those are only unconfirmed speculations. Nowadays, nobody knows the treacherous passages through the dangerous reefs to reach the isle of Nargor.
pl_reference_issues.pl: Wyjąca Grota w Nargorze była kryjówką przestępców na początku, kiedy na wyspach dopiero rozpoczęła się kolonizacja. Przestępcy ci byli prawdopodobnie pierwszymi piratami, chociaż jest mało prawdopodobne, aby mieli do dyspozycji więcej niż kilka łodzi rybackich. Zbudowali w jaskiniach kilka pomieszczeń, ale podobno znaleźli dowody wcześniejszych prób wykorzystania groty w jakiś sposób, a niektóre jaskinie wydawały się nienaturalne. Z jakiegoś powodu przyciągały ich niższe jaskinie, gdzie wycie wiatru było tak gwałtowne, że ludzie mówili, że może doprowadzić człowieka do szaleństwa. Tak czy inaczej, ci pierwsi piraci byli znani ze swojej żądzy krwi, częstych walk wewnętrznych i torturowania więźniów. Zakłada się, że wszyscy w swoim szaleństwie popełnili samobójstwo. Krążą pogłoski, że grotę nawiedzają duchy tych piratów i ich ofiar – są to jednak tylko niepotwierdzone spekulacje. W dzisiejszych czasach nikt nie zna zdradliwych przejść przez niebezpieczne rafy, które prowadzą na wyspę Nargor.
pl_reference_issues.lang: The Howling Grotto of Nargor used to be a hideout for criminals in the early days when colonisation just started on the isles. Those criminals were probably the first pirates although is unlikely that they had more than a few fishing boats at their disposal. They built some rooms in the caverns but supposedly they found evidence of prior attempts to use the grotto in some way and some of the caverns seemed to be not natural. For some reasons they were attracted to the lower caves where the howling of the wind was that fierce that people said it could drive a man crazy. Be that as it may, those first pirates were known for their bloodthirst, their frequent infightings and for torturing their prisoners. It is assumed that they all killed themselves in their madness. The grotto is rumoured to be haunted by the ghosts of these pirates and those of their victims - but those are only unconfirmed speculations. Nowadays, nobody knows the treacherous passages through the dangerous reefs to reach the isle of Nargor.
